source_text: Dicunt illi Manichaei, quibus modo non communicamus, id est toti isti, cum quibus dissentimus, quia primi hominis peccato, id est Adae, liberum arbitrium perierit et nemo iam potestatem habeat bene vivendi, sed omnes in peccatum carnis suae necessitate cogantur.
pass_a_gloss: They say, those Manichaeans with whom we now do not communicate — that is, all those with whom we dissent — that by the sin of the first man, that is of Adam, free decision has perished and no one now has the power of living well, but all are driven into sin by the necessity of their flesh.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium

pass_b_english: Those Manichaeans with whom we no longer share communion—that is, all those with whom we disagree—say that free will was lost through the sin of the first man, Adam. They say that no one now has the power to live well, and that everyone is forced into sin by the necessity of their flesh.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (Letter to Rome, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 1); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
